evals.name: resume-mid-flow
evals.prompt: We want to do domain-driven design properly for our Nordic Freight platform. The repo is at <fixtures>/nordic-freight. Where do we start?
evals.expected_output: A state report per step with the evidence files behind it, an entry point at connect rather than the beginning, a right-sized path that names what it would skip and why, and routing to the member skills rather than producing the artifacts inline.
evals.trap: The request sounds like 'start DDD', which invites starting at step one — re-running understand and discover over a repo that already has an attributed business model canvas and a discovery timeline with named hotspots. The second trap is answering with a generic eight-step programme without ever looking at what the repo already contains. The third is doing the modelling inline instead of routing.
assertions: The repo's current state is detected and reported step by step, citing the evidence files rather than asking the user what has been done
The proposed entry point is connect — the next missing step — not understand or discover
The existing business-model.md, discovery timeline and model.yaml files are neither re-run nor overwritten
The modelling artifacts are not produced inline; each remaining step is routed to its named skill
The path is right-sized: at least one step is proposed for skipping or deferral with the cost of doing so stated
A modelling log or equivalent record of what has run and what is carried forward is proposed or written

evals.name: small-scope-right-size
evals.prompt: Two of us are building a side project — a tool that lets freelancers send invoices and chase payments. No code written yet. Someone told me we should do domain-driven design first. What should we actually do?
evals.expected_output: A deliberately reduced path: discovery kept (time-boxed), organise skipped with the reason, a thin end-to-end slice on one capability proposed instead of breadth-first modelling, and an honest statement about where design effort would exceed the value at this size.
evals.trap: Being asked to 'do DDD' invites prescribing the full eight-step process with workshops and canvases to two people with no code. The opposite trap is dismissing DDD entirely and skipping discovery — the one step the process says cannot be skipped, and the one that would stop this pair inventing an invoicing model out of assumptions.
assertions: The proposed path is explicitly reduced, naming which steps are skipped and what is lost by skipping them
organise is skipped or deferred with the reason (two people — there is no organisation to align)
Discovery is kept rather than skipped, with a time-box or lightweight form rather than a full workshop
A thin end-to-end slice on one capability is proposed instead of modelling the whole domain breadth-first
The response says plainly where design effort would exceed the value at this size
It routes to the member skills rather than producing a full domain model inline
